questions.question: What is a finite sequence of the form $(a_i)_{i = 0}^n$?
options: A sequence indexed by all real numbers.
A sequence with no last term.
A sequence with indices ending at a natural number $n$.
A sequence whose terms must all be equal.

questions.question: What is true for finite sequences?
options: Finite sequences never have a first term.
Finite sequences have a last term.
Finite sequences cannot be viewed as functions.

questions.question: Which is an example of a finite sequence?
How many terms does $(a_i)_{i = 1}^1$ have?
How can every finite sequence be viewed?
options: As a function on all of $\mathbb{R}$.
As a function on a finite index set.
As a set with no order information.

questions.question: Why are finite sequences always bounded?
options: They contain only finitely many terms.

questions.question: For $(a_i)_{i = 0}^3$, which term is the last term?
Which sequence notation most directly indicates a finite sequence?
Which statement best distinguishes a finite sequence from a finite set?
options: A finite sequence can never have repeated values
A finite sequence cannot be bounded.
A finite sequence has indexed terms; order and position matter
A finite sequence has no last term.

questions.question: Why does the existence of a last term matter for finite sequences?
options: It reflects that the index stops at a final natural number
It shows that the sequence must be infinite.
It means the first term is undefined.
It prevents the sequence from being a function

questions.question: A sequence is given by $(a_i)_{i = 1}^4 = (1,\,-3,\,2,\,7)$. Which statement is guaranteed by the definition?
options: It is indexed by all natural numbers.

questions.question: If a sequence is viewed as a function on the finite index set $\{1,2,3\}$, which output corresponds to index $2$ in $(5,\,8,\,13)$?
What feature makes a sequence finite?
options: It is indexed by all natural numbers forever.
All its terms must be different.

questions.question: Why does order matter in a finite sequence?
options: Its terms form an unordered set.
Its terms are indexed by positions.

questions.question: Which property is guaranteed for every finite sequence?
How many terms are in $(a_i)_{i=2}^{4}$?
What is the last term of $(b_j)_{j=1}^{7}$?
Is $(5,5,5)$ a finite sequence?
options: No, finite sequences cannot repeat values.
Yes, but only if all terms are distinct.

questions.question: How can a finite sequence be viewed as a function?
options: As a function from all real numbers to itself.
As an unordered subset of $\mathbb{R}$ only.
As a function with no domain under the stated limiting assumptions.
As a function from a finite index set to the set of possible term values.
